thread:
aditya: quick sync — i've got an RFC follow-up draft on local controlplane exposure patterns. need a short decision on DNS delegation vs in-band proxying for customers who block zone delegations.

lucy: is this mainly for onboarding new private tenants or for a migration path from global->local?

aditya: both. onboarding first; migration later. the tricky bit is cert and src-ip expectations for enterprise customers.

marco: two quick options: 1) DNS delegation: operator creates a delegated zone in customer's account (preferred for low-latency and native cert SAN). 2) Proxy endpoint: operator keeps DNS, agent switches to operator-managed proxy that rewrites Host header and mints proxy certs.

grace: delegation fails when customers deny zone delegation. proxy works but breaks source IP for egress ACLs. can we do hybrid: attempt delegation, if denied, request an ENI attach; if ENI unavailable, fall back to proxy?

aditya: hybrid seems pragmatic. but ENI attach has cross-account permission hurdles and adds cost. we need a clear fallback policy and an explicit customer opt-in for ENI.

marco: security note: proxy approach must avoid header-spoofing risk. don't rely on unsigned headers. use signed proxy attestations and ephemeral proxy certs issued by a short-lived intermediate that only relays can use. include tenant id and original SAN in the cert extension.

security-bot: reminder: any proxy-cert flow must include revocation / rotation controls and documented TTLs.

lucy: also consider audit: customers want cryptographic proof that requests came from their agents when using a relay. we can sign attestations for each attach/cutover event and publish to tenant audit logs (optionally S3).

aditya: proposal for cutover sequence (hybrid):
1) try zone delegation. if success -> agent uses local DNS and fetches cert as usual.
2) if delegation blocked -> try ENI attach via assume-role (15m) with strict tag condition. if attach succeeds -> create local endpoint + stable src-ip.
3) if attach blocked or denied -> provision regional relay and enable proxy-cert issuance. agent uses relay path and receives ephemeral cert.
4) operator emits signed attestation event for whatever path used and increments metrics.

marco: need to define attestation format: include tenant_id, path_type (delegation|eni|relay), timestamp, operator_job_id, and signature. customers can verify with our published key.

lucy: config sketch to ship in RFC follow-up:```yaml
tenant: example-llc
controlplane_preference: [delegation, eni, relay] # ordered fallback
eni_request_role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-eni-attach # optional
narrow_eni_permissions: true
proxy_cert_ttl_seconds: 300
publish_attestations: true
```

grace: operational metrics: delegation_attempts, eni_attach_attempts, relay_provisions, attestation_emitted, proxy_cert_errors, srcip_fallback_count. we also need an emergency manual-cutover API to pin route to relay or local.

aditya: rollback semantics: if dual-session period exists, ensure local plane is read-only; all mutations route to global plane to avoid split-brain. dual-session TTL = 60s default. manual rollback requires operator approval for "required" tenants.

marco: edge-case: what about tenants that require preserved src-ip even on relay? we could offer a per-tenant egress-NAT pool (ENI held by operator in customer account) but mark as enterprise-only paid feature. document cost and latency tradeoffs.

security-bot: flagged item: ensure assume-role used for ENI attach restricts to subnet ARNs and aws:ResourceTag/tenant-id conditions. add requirement to RFC.

lucy: testing matrix: delegation success/failure, ENI attach policy-deny, ENI attach transient error, relay cert rotation, mass-failover simulation (1000 tenants). include e2e test verifying attestation signature and audit log entry.

aditya: plan: i'll produce the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, attestation schema, config snippet, and a short runbook. recommend default = delegation->relay (skip ENI unless tenant opts into eni mode). tagging @marco @grace for quick review. :+1:
